en: The Chapter on Similes, Section on the Lion (Sīhavagga)
8. The Question on the Leech “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘one quality of the leech should be adopted,’ which is that one quality that should be adopted?
“Just as, great king, the leech, wherever it attaches itself, clings firmly right there and drinks blood;”
In the same way, great king, when a practitioner of yoga has a mind that clings to an object, he should firmly establish that object by way of its color,
shape, direction, location, boundaries, characteristic marks, and signs; and by means of that very object,
he should drink the overflowing nectar of liberation.
This, Great King, is one quality that should be adopted from the leech.
This was also said, Great King, by the Elder Anuruddha:
“With a mind that is utterly pure...”
Having established oneself upon the object,
one should drink with that mind the sprinkling of the flavor of liberation.”
The eighth question: on the leech-limbs.
